lines: People paste client documents into AI.
scenes.vo: Every day, people paste client contracts, bank letters and payslips into ChatGPT. Every name, address and account number in them goes straight to the model provider.

scenes.label: Veil
scenes.vo: Veil fixes that. It hides the personal data in a document before any AI sees it, and puts the real values back in the answer.

scenes.label: 1. Drop a document
scenes.vo: Here is a four page tenancy agreement, full of names, addresses and phone numbers. A detector model, trained and served through Mubit, reads it part by part, next to a rules layer for UK numbers.

scenes.label: 2. Review what is hidden
scenes.vo: In a few seconds, every name, address and number is blacked out. In the PDF you download, the text under each box is removed from the file, not just covered.

scenes.label: Every part is a Mubit call
scenes.vo: Each part of the document was its own call to Mubit, and every request id is right here.

scenes.label: 3. Fix a miss
scenes.vo: Missed something? The landlord is our client, so I select the company name and hide it. That correction is exactly what Mubit trains the next version of the model on.

scenes.label: 4. Approve
scenes.vo: Only when I approve can the document go to an AI.

scenes.label: 5. Ask the AI
scenes.vo: I ask when the landlord can raise the rent. Claude only sees placeholders, like person one, and Veil puts the real names back on my laptop.

scenes.label: What the AI received
scenes.vo: And this is exactly what the AI received. No names, no addresses, no account numbers.

scenes.label: Results
scenes.vo: On our synthetic test set, rules alone hide thirty eight percent of personal values, and not a single name or address. The adapter we trained in Mubit passed ninety two percent of its held out test, against sixty seven for the base model.

lines: Your documents stay inside the walls.
scenes.vo: Every correction makes your own privacy model better, and your clients' data never reaches the model provider. Veil.
